en: Theragāthā 6.9 Chakkanipāta,
Paṭhamavagga (The First Chapter)
The Verses of the Elder Jenta, Son of the Family Priest:
“I was intoxicated with pride in my birth,
and with wealth and power;”
Intoxicated by my pride in my physical form and complexion,
I did not treat anyone as my equal.
And he conceives himself as superior;
struck by overweening pride, the fool is stiff-necked and has his banner raised high.
I did not pay homage to my mother,
nor to my father, nor to anyone else who was esteemed as venerable.
Stubborn in his pride and disrespectful,
he saw the Leader, the supreme and most excellent of charioteers.
Like the scorching sun,
honored by the community of monks;
having cast aside pride and intoxication,
With a serene mind,
I paid homage with my head to the one supreme among all beings.
Excessive pride and self-contempt have been abandoned and thoroughly uprooted;
the conceit "I am" has been utterly severed.
“All types of conceit have been destroyed.
… The Elder Jenta, son of the family priest …
